lines: codex_top_seat() {
local NAME="$1" ROLE="$2" USE="$3" SIZE="$4" KEY="$5" BRIEF="$6" DEST="$7" OUT RC ACT="" TRY TO MDL; shift 7
local SEAT="$HOME/.claude/skills/_meta/seat_model.py" QUOTA="$HOME/.claude/skills/_meta/codex_quota.py"
local WATCH="$HOME/.claude/skills/_meta/codex_watch.py" TRIES="1 2" SUBUSE="$USE" RETRY RRC RTO AID="" AKEY=""
local L2 WA RIN UU UK UM
# The receipt: `<admission id> <key>` of this seat's LIVE admission, written atomically by argv. DEST must be
# unique per seat (the receipt is "$DEST.admit"). Read in a subshell, so this function's "$@" is untouched.
rm -f "$DEST.admit"
# SIZE and KEY are EMPTY when the caller has none, and an empty one passes NO FLAG AT ALL. Sizing is
# opt-in: with no --size the registry reads no size file, so an unsized seat takes the TOP model even on
# a small cycle -- and passing a literal size instead of nothing would record `size_source: routing`, a
# routing decision nobody made. An empty KEY leaves the budget key the project derives; a caller that
# mints its own passes it here, so its seats share ONE key and spend their OWN budget, not the round's.
# #322: --await-quota -- a QUOTA refusal records no stand-in yet; it prints the reset lines and
# `substitution=deferred`, and the seat's owner waits (see CODEX_QUOTA_WAIT below).
OUT="$(python3 "$SEAT" argv --role "$ROLE" --provider codex --use "$USE" --receipt-file "$DEST.admit" \
--await-quota ${SIZE:+--size "$SIZE"} ${KEY:+--cycle-id "$KEY"} \
--project-root "${PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}")"; RC=$?
# The timeout is the seat registry's, asked only AFTER an admitted `argv --use` (asked first, a no-eligible
# substitution would become a gap) and never as a second `argv` stdout line: $OUT is word-split into
# `codex exec $OUT`, so an extra line would become a prompt. No timeout -> the gap line; codex never runs.
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
TO="$(python3 "$SEAT" timeout --role "$ROLE" --provider codex)" || { ACT="seat_model timeout exit $?"; RC=1; }
MDL="$(set -- $OUT; echo "$2")"     # the pinned model, named once: progress line and substitution record
AID="$(set -- $(cat "$DEST.admit" 2>/dev/null); echo "${1-}")"
AKEY="$(set -- $(cat "$DEST.admit" 2>/dev/null); echo "${2-}")"; AKEY="${AKEY:-$KEY}"
fi
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
while [ -n "$TRIES" ]; do
for TRY in $TRIES; do
# D24: the watchdog stops the call on INACTIVITY -- no stdout, no stderr and no session-rollout write
# for the idle window -- so "thinking hard" is no longer killed as "hung". The registry timeout is
# passed as the RUNAWAY cap only, never as the normal stop, and the watchdog prints a progress line to
# this call's stderr while it waits. Its exits: 111 went silent (the retryable stop, classified as a
# timeout), 112 ran away while still active (a gap on the FIRST hit, never a substitution), anything
# else is codex's own status passed straight through.
python3 "$WATCH" --mode codex --hard-cap "$TO" --model "$MDL" \
--stdout-file "$DEST.stdout" --stderr-file "$DEST.stderr" \
-- codex exec "$@" $OUT -o "$DEST" "$(cat "$BRIEF")"; RC=$?
ACT="$(python3 "$QUOTA" classify --exit-code "$RC" --attempt "$TRY" $([ "$RC" -eq 111 ] && echo --timed-out) \
--stderr-file "$DEST.stderr" --output-file "$DEST" --prompt-file "$BRIEF")" || ACT=classify_error
[ "${ACT%% *}" = retry ] || break
done
TRIES=""
# U2, the astra reserve: a seat that failed on CAPABILITY (capacity or a malformed answer, twice) gets ONE
# attempt on the codex TOP. seat_model decides whether that is a retry at all -- it proves the failed
# attempt from its receipt (an admitted std row of this role, use and key), wants a DIFFERENT pin that
# bills the TOP class, and admits it as `top_retry` on the FORGE CYCLE (1 per cycle) -- and records the
# event row. The TOP timeout is asked FIRST, so a failed lookup spends no retry slot. Exit 0: run it ONCE,
# classified as attempt 2 so it has no inner retry, and SUBUSE stops a second entry; the receipt now names
# the retry's own admission and key. Exit 3: the D6 line, already recorded. Anything else: the original
# failure is substituted below. Quota, auth, budget, timeout and gap outcomes never reach this branch.
case "$SUBUSE:$ACT" in
"$USE:substitute capacity_twice"|"$USE:substitute malformed_twice")
RRC=1
if RTO="$(python3 "$SEAT" timeout --role "$ROLE" --provider codex --top-retry)"; then
rm -f "$DEST.admit"   # only the retry's own receipt may follow
RETRY="$(python3 "$SEAT" argv --role "$ROLE" --provider codex --use "$USE" --top-retry \
--failed-admission-id "$AID" --failed-reason "${ACT#substitute }" \
--receipt-file "$DEST.admit" --await-quota ${AKEY:+--cycle-id "$AKEY"} \
--project-root "${PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}")"; RRC=$?
fi
if [ "$RRC" -eq 0 ]; then
OUT="$RETRY"; MDL="$(set -- $OUT; echo "$2")"; SUBUSE=top_retry; TRIES=2; TO="$RTO"
AKEY="$(set -- $(cat "$DEST.admit" 2>/dev/null); echo "${2-}")"; AKEY="${AKEY:-$KEY}"
elif [ "$RRC" -eq 3 ]; then
OUT="$RETRY"; ACT=top_retry_substituted
fi ;;
esac
done
case "$ACT" in
top_retry_substituted) RC=3 ;;
# the substitution names the key its admission was billed to (the receipt's, else the caller's KEY): a
# failed TOP retry keeps its forge-cycle key, a tournament or ballot seat its own
"substitute "*) OUT="$(python3 "$SEAT" substitute --role "$ROLE" --use "$SUBUSE" --reason "${ACT#substitute }" \
--requested-model "$MDL" ${AKEY:+--cycle-id "$AKEY"} \
--project-root "${PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}")"; RC=$? ;;
# classify itself failed: after a codex exit 0 keep codex's output in $DEST; after a failed call, a gap
classify_error) if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
echo "CODEX_CLASSIFY_ERROR: $NAME: classify failed after codex exit 0; $DEST keeps its output" >&2
else RC=1; fi ;;
esac
fi
# Exit 3 prints the reason on LINE 1 and the Claude model on LINE 2; a quota refusal (#322) appends
# key=value lines after them, so the model is read as line 2, never as the last line.
case "$RC:$OUT" in
0:*) ;;  # codex answered: $DEST holds its output
3:*$'\n'substitution=deferred*)
WA="${OUT##*$'\n'wait_advice=}"; WA="${WA%%$'\n'*}"

RIN="unknown"; case "$OUT" in *$'
'resets_in_s=*) RIN="${OUT##*$'
'resets_in_s=}"; RIN="${RIN%%$'
'*}" ;; esac
# #322 fix round 1: the use, key and codex model a later `substitute` must name (a TOP retry's own)

UM="-"; case "$OUT" in *$'
'requested_model=*) UM="${OUT##*$'
'requested_model=}"; UM="${UM%%$'
'*}" ;; esac
printf 'CODEX_QUOTA_WAIT: %s (reason %s; wait_advice %s; resets_in_s %s; stand-in %s; use %s; key %s; requested %s)\nbrief: %s\n' \
"$NAME" "${OUT%%$'\n'*}" "$WA" "$RIN" "$L2" "$UU" "$UK" "$UM" "$BRIEF" > "$DEST" ;;
3:*) printf 'CODEX_SUBSTITUTE: %s -> %s (reason %s; provider gap: openai)\nbrief: %s\n' \
*) echo "CODEX_GAP: $NAME seat skipped (${ACT:-exit $RC}; see stderr)" > "$DEST" ;;
esac

**SANDBOX RULE (S052 rogue-commit incident, #157):** the agy analyst is a READ-ONLY role — ALWAYS
invoke it with `--sandbox`. agy has write/shell/git tools by default; in S052 an un-sandboxed
"analyst" auto-authored and git-committed broken code mid-design (HARD-GATE violation). Codex is
unaffected (it already runs `-s read-only`). FLAG ORDER (root-caused 2026-07-02): `--sandbox` and
every other flag BEFORE `-p`, prompt LAST — `agy -p --sandbox "X"` silently runs UN-sandboxed
with the literal prompt `--sandbox` and discards "X" (agy then improvises from implicit memory —
the "does work instead of consulting" failure mode). Scope caveat (verified 2026-07-02, 1.0.15):
`--sandbox` constrains shell/git only, NOT native file writes — prefer piping content over
`--add-dir` on a writable repo, open the prompt with "Advisory only — do not modify any files;
answer on stdout", and run `git status --short` afterwards if a repo was exposed.
&& timeout 600 agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL -p "You are an analyst for [TASK].
At the very end print one line: SERVED_BY=<model-id-you-are-running-as>." < /dev/null
# For codebase context, add the relevant paths to the workspace with --add-dir:
# CAUTION: --sandbox does NOT gate native file writes into --add-dir trees — prefer piping;
# if you must --add-dir a writable repo, run `git status --short` afterwards and revert strays.
&& timeout 600 agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL --add-dir [PATHS] -p "Advisory only — do not modify any files; answer on stdout.
Review the codebase at [PATHS] for [TASK].
Focus on: cross-cutting concerns, hidden coupling, N+1 patterns, missing error boundaries." < /dev/null
&& timeout 600 agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL -p "Brainstorm approaches for [TASK] using the Six Thinking Hats methodology —
Green (alternatives), and Blue (process) in turn, then summarise." < /dev/null

The lead never closes one.

User says fix: a `--user-directed` round citing their words as `--user-ref`. User says leave it: `unfixable: contradicts a standing user decision`, quoting the ruling, so step 4 stays the only path to done with one open.

## Worked example: an owner statement widened into a rule (`constraint-question`)
The retro behind step 5, replayed with its real inputs. A consumer project's forge cycle existed to improve local SEO.
- **Owner:** "we allow local collection but no show room."

- **Constraint as the lead wrote it:** never write "visit", "shop", "store", "showroom" or shop opening hours. Labelled, it splits: the showroom wording is `owner-stated: "we allow local collection but no show room."`; the opening-hours clause adds to what the owner said, so it is `lead-inferred`.
- **Finding:** a **minor** from a fresh **Claude** reviewer, marked **owner decision**: the `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD is `ComputerStore` with `openingHoursSpecification` Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00.

**What happened:** the citation was real, so every check passed, and the lead relayed the finding with "I'd remove", in the sign-off for a release whose purpose was local search. The owner caught it with one question.
**Replay:**
1. Steps 1-4: the citation matches. **VERIFIED.**
2. Step 5 still applies: being a minor, from a Claude reviewer, on an owner-decision item exempts it from nothing.
3. Without the `lead-inferred` clause the hours contradict nothing, so the finding exists only because of that clause. **`constraint-question`.** It is not ruled and no fix is proposed.

4. It reaches the owner as a question about the constraint: "The brief says no shop opening hours. That clause is mine, not yours: you said no show room. Did you mean the hours too? Effect on the Purpose: not evaluated." No recommendation goes with it.
5. Report header: `goal-fit: 0 ruled, 0 works-against, 1 constraint-question`.

If the owner rejects the clause, the finding closes with their words quoted and the hours stay. If they confirm it, it becomes `owner-stated: "<quote>"` and the finding is ruled normally. While the hours are true, removing them harms the Purpose, so the fix is `works-against` and takes the route in step 5. If the owner says the hours are false, the markup is a claim false on owner-stated facts, which is never ruled `works-against`, so it takes the normal fix path.
## Worked example: a genuine trade-off (`works-against`, illustrative)
**Purpose:** `owner-stated: "the status page must load instantly on a bad connection"`.

**Finding (major, Codex, VERIFIED):** the page serves a snapshot up to five minutes old with no age shown, so a reader can take a resolved incident for a live one. Proposed fix: drop the snapshot and fetch live on every view.

**Ruling:** no `lead-inferred` constraint is involved, and the finding is not on the never-ruled list. The defect is real and the fix is `works-against`: "the status page must load instantly on a bad connection", and a live fetch puts a round trip on the bad connection before anything renders.

**Route, when another fix exists:** keep the snapshot, show its age and refresh it in the background. That resolves the defect without harming the Purpose. The finding is a major, so this is the fix, with no approval step, and the swap is recorded.

**Route, when none exists:** suppose instead the finding were that readers need per-region detail the snapshot cannot hold, so every fix adds the round trip. It goes to the user labelled `works-against`, with both sides and no default fix. If it is the last blocker the round is recorded `awaiting-user`; otherwise the round stays `fixing`, or `exhausted` at the bound. The finding is carried in `--raised` and `--verified` on every later row. The user says fix (a `--user-directed` round) or leave it (`unfixable: contradicts a standing user decision`, quoting the ruling).
